body:
Globulation 2 gains a desktop browser client built from the native engine: WebGL2/software rendering, campaigns and custom games, an editor, durable browser saves, import/export, and YOG cross-play through a WebSocket gateway. This replaces #203 and consolidates the port onto current master `a494a3319`.

The browser implementation uses scheduled screens and cooperative loading without Asyncify. The shared source manifest and isolated SCons build identities support native client/server, router, gateway, and WebAssembly builds. Native WSS remains optional with `wss=0`. Build and play instructions are in [browser/README.md](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/blob/browser-platform/browser/README.md).

The cleanup fixes concrete failures found during integration:

- Removes the old grass/cloud menu renderer and prevents an outgoing screen from drawing after a child changes the frontend style. Modern colony backgrounds survive game exits and nested menus.
- Rejects native preview-worker results for slots removed by a restart; the old code produces an AddressSanitizer container overflow. Browser autosaves drain without trying to create unsupported threads, and loading telemetry no longer spans cooperative suspensions.
- Checks WebGL's actual context state before rendering, including the interval before the context-loss event arrives, and restores GPU resources while retaining the session.
- Copies complete replay recordings from both memory and file backends, preserves trailing idle ticks, and opens recordings in binary mode on Windows. Browser tests follow the current custom-game controls and select the named replay recording.

Review follow-up fixes keep Settings open until the latest write is durable, drain native TCP bursts without per-message waits, and restore native resize polling while keeping server builds independent of graphics. Each regression fails against the prior implementation and passes with the fix. [Before/after logs and reproduction sources](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/evidence/browser-platform-379/regressions/review-fixes) include 21 passing Chromium/Firefox/WebKit settings tests and native transport, resize, screen lifecycle, and settings checks. The native settings retry harness now runs in Linux CI. Session reload tests now retain the named save instead of accidentally selecting a newly created autosave; all three focused WebGL session tests pass locally. [Updated-head CI](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36061582543) passes all nine jobs on `262e63ec0`; complete logs and final platform replay artifacts are retained with the review-fix evidence.

Network protocol **41** covers the versioned server greeting and symmetric admission: update native clients and YOG servers together for cross-play. Save and replay format floors remain those of master. Shared lifecycle and native build-output changes are part of this PR, so it needs review beyond the browser adapter.

Validation and downloadable artifacts are on the [review evidence branch](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/tree/evidence/browser-platform-379):

- [All nine CI jobs pass](https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/36061582543): Linux GCC 11/13, Windows, native build variants and generator checks, browser/deployment, and simulation equivalence. Browser results: **94** Chromium software tests, **20** Firefox/WebKit software tests, **22** focused Chromium WebGL2 tests (one software-only skip), and both real-window visibility checks. Real TLS routing and persistent-volume deployment tests pass.
- The master macOS arm64 build, rebased native build, Linux GCC 11/13, Windows, and WebAssembly produce byte-identical per-tick traces for `games/cross-replay.game`, seed 42, 1,500 ticks. SHA-256: `110443ab4a136dff6621f32dbeed150a15c18394791874e3774ef6cbe27c3c48`. CI compares its four platform traces automatically. This fixture does not establish equivalence for every game or generator.
- Local Chromium on Metal: **91 passed, 1 intentional skip**; focused Firefox/WebKit software: **28 passed**. Torus switching and actual context restoration pass on Metal and SwiftShader. Multiplayer coverage includes browser/browser and matching browser/native checkpoints over TCP and WSS.
- Native screen/session, save safety, custom setup and previews, unit continuation, protocol admission, TCP/WSS, gateway, build isolation, Maxima, and tournament CLI checks pass. Evidence includes before/after transition, preview-thread, and replay-export regressions, saved games/replays, UI screenshots, and complete CI logs.

Browser defaults use the system cursor, muted audio, and reduced effects. Map generation yields between preview candidates; an individual roll remains synchronous and can pause the UI. Mobile controls, reconnect recovery, and website deployment are outside this PR. Linux WebKit WebGL2 high-density resizing remains an intermittent validation failure; use `?renderer=software` if affected. WebKit automation does not replace shipping Safari playtesting. Actual Windows modal dragging was not repeated locally for the review fixes; automated resize coverage passes.
title: Add the browser platform with durable saves and YOG cross-play
